title: A 24-Vertex Oriented Graph Showing f(4) ≥ 5/4 in a Source-Neighborhood Problem for Quasi-Kernels
abstract: For a vertex $v$ of a sourceless digraph, let $S(v)$ be the set of sources of $D - N^+[v]$ and let $E(v) = N^+(v) \cup N^+(S(v))$. Problem 5.2 of arXiv:2601.11847 asks, for each $d \ge 2$, for the least constant $f(d)$ such that every sourceless oriented graph of maximum out-degree at most $d$ has a vertex $v$ with $f(d)|E(v)| \ge |S(v)| + 1$, and for the least $d$ with $f(d) > 1$. We give an explicit loopless sourceless oriented graph on 24 vertices with maximum out-degree four in which every vertex satisfies $5|E(v)| \le 4(|S(v)|+1)$: the eight non-sink vertices have $|S(v)| = |E(v)| = 4$ and the sixteen sinks have $S(v) = E(v) = \emptyset$. Hence $f(4) \ge 5/4$, and the least $d$ with $f(d) > 1$ is at most 4; if the paper's Conjecture 5.1 (the case $d = 3$ with constant 1) holds, it is exactly 4. The graph is an instance of the paper's construction for Proposition 2.3, sink leaves attached to a regular core, with a 2-diregular oriented core on eight vertices in place of the regular tournament, which that construction needs on at least seven vertices to beat ratio 1. The same graph has a quasi-kernel of six vertices. All properties are verified in Lean 4.
introduction:
A quasi-kernel of a digraph $D$ is an independent set $Q$ such that every vertex is reached from $Q$ by a directed path of length at most two. Every digraph has one, and the Small Quasi-Kernel Conjecture asserts that every sourceless digraph on $n$ vertices has one of size at most $n/2$.

The paper arXiv:2601.11847 approaches the conjecture through a smallest counterexample. For a vertex $v$, deleting the closed out-neighbourhood $N^+[v] = \{v\} \cup N^+(v)$ may create sources; write $S(v)$ for the set of sources of $D - N^+[v]$ and
\[
E(v) = N^+(v) \cup N^+(S(v)).
\]
Its Algorithm 1 builds a quasi-kernel from a vertex $v$ and a quasi-kernel of a smaller sourceless digraph, and the resulting criterion is: if every sourceless digraph has a vertex with $t|E(v)| \ge |S(v)| + 1$, quasi-kernels of size at most $tn/(t+1)$ follow, so $t = 1$ would give the conjecture. The paper proves a $4n/7$ bound for maximum out-degree three this way, conjectures (Conjecture 5.1) that every sourceless oriented graph of maximum out-degree at most three has a vertex with $|E(v)| \ge |S(v)| + 1$, and shows (Proposition 2.3) that without a degree bound no constant works: for every $c > 0$ there is a sourceless digraph in which every non-sink vertex has $c|E(v)| < |S(v)| + 1$.

Problem 5.2 of the paper asks how far the method goes at bounded degree: for fixed $d \ge 2$, what is the least constant $f(d)$ such that every sourceless oriented graph of maximum out-degree at most $d$ has a vertex $v$ with
\[
f(d)\,|E(v)| \ge |S(v)| + 1,
\]
and what is the least $d$ such that $f(d) > 1$? A lower bound $f(d) \ge c$ is a single sourceless oriented graph of maximum out-degree at most $d$ in which no vertex satisfies the inequality for any constant below $c$.

The construction behind Proposition 2.3 takes a regular tournament on $2n+1$ vertices in which no out-neighbourhood equals an in-neighbourhood and attaches $k$ private sinks to each vertex; every non-sink vertex then has $|S(v)| = nk$ and $|E(v)| = n + k$, so the ratio is $(nk+1)/(n+k)$ at out-degree $n + k$. The ratio exceeds 1 only when $n, k \ge 2$; for $n = 2$ the regular tournament on five vertices has a vertex whose out-neighbourhood is another vertex's in-neighbourhood, so the smallest case is the seven-vertex Paley tournament with two sinks per vertex, which gives $f(5) \ge 7/5$.

We go one degree lower. Replacing the tournament by an eight-vertex oriented graph in which every vertex has in- and out-degree two, and attaching two private sinks to each core vertex, gives a 24-vertex sourceless oriented graph of maximum out-degree four in which every core vertex has $|S(v)| = |E(v)| = 4$ and every sink has $S(v) = E(v) = \emptyset$. The Lean theorem `digraph_four_outdegree_five_four_counterexample` states that every vertex satisfies $5|E(v)| \le 4(|S(v)|+1)$. Hence $f(4) \ge 5/4$ and the least $d$ with $f(d) > 1$ is at most four. Since a graph of maximum out-degree at most two also has maximum out-degree at most three, Conjecture 5.1 would give $f(2), f(3) \le 1$, and then the least such $d$ is exactly four. The theorem also exhibits a quasi-kernel of six vertices in the same graph, so the failure of the local criterion here says nothing against the conjecture itself.
result:
The main theorem established and verified in Lean 4 is the existence of the 24-vertex witness:

\begin{theorem}[`digraph_four_outdegree_five_four_counterexample`]
There exists an out-neighborhood function $\text{out} : \text{Fin } 24 \to \text{Finset } (\text{Fin } 24)$ defining a directed graph such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\text{out}$ is loopless: $\forall v,\ v \notin \text{out}(v)$.
\item $\text{out}$ is source-free: $\forall v,\ \exists u,\ v \in \text{out}(u)$.
\item $\text{out}$ is oriented: $\forall u, v,\ v \in \text{out}(u) \implies u \notin \text{out}(v)$.
\item The maximum outdegree is at most 4: $\forall v,\ |\text{out}(v)| \le 4$.
\item For every vertex $v$, the local source set $S(v)$ and the local source expansion set $E(v)$ satisfy:
\[
|E(v)| = |S(v)| \quad \text{and} \quad 5 |E(v)| \le 4 (|S(v)| + 1).
\]
\item There exists an independent two-step out-dominating set $Q \subseteq \text{Fin } 24$ of cardinality exactly 6:
\[
|Q| = 6 \quad \text{and} \quad (\forall u, v \in Q,\ u \neq v \implies v \notin \text{out}(u))
\]
\[
\text{and} \quad (\forall v,\ \exists u \in Q,\ u = v \lor v \in \text{out}(u) \lor \exists w \in \text{out}(u),\ v \in \text{out}(w)).
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

In Lean 4, the theorem is stated as:
```lean
theorem digraph_four_outdegree_five_four_counterexample :
    ∃ out : Fin 24 → Finset (Fin 24),
      (∀ v, v ∉ out v) ∧
      (∀ v, ∃ u, v ∈ out u) ∧
      (∀ u v, v ∈ out u → u ∉ out v) ∧
      (∀ v, (out v).card ≤ 4) ∧
      (∀ v, (digraph_local_source_expansion out v).card = (digraph_local_source_set out v).card ∧
        5 * (digraph_local_source_expansion out v).card ≤ 4 * ((digraph_local_source_set out v).card + 1)) ∧
      (∃ Q : Finset (Fin 24), Q.card = 6 ∧
        (∀ u ∈ Q, ∀ v ∈ Q, u ≠ v → v ∉ out u) ∧
        (∀ v, ∃ u ∈ Q, u = v ∨ v ∈ out u ∨ ∃ w, w ∈ out u ∧ v ∈ out w))
```
The Lean formulation asserts the existence of an out-neighborhood map on the 24-element type `Fin 24`, conjunctively verifying the five structural conditions alongside the existence of the 6-element quasi-kernel $Q$.

Problem 5.2 asks for a vertex with $f|E(v)| \ge |S(v)| + 1$. In this graph no vertex has one when $f < 5/4$: at a sink, $|E(v)| = 0 < 1 = |S(v)| + 1$; at a core vertex, $f|E(v)| < \tfrac54|E(v)| \le |S(v)| + 1$ by the theorem, since $|E(v)| = 4 > 0$. Thus $f(4) \ge 5/4$; at the core vertices $5|E(v)| = 20 = 4(|S(v)|+1)$, so the constant $5/4$ itself is attained by this graph and the bound cannot be improved using it. In particular $f(4) > 1$, so the least $d$ with $f(d) > 1$ in Problem 5.2 is at most four. The quasi-kernel $Q$ has $6 = 24/4$ vertices, well within the conjectured $n/2$.
proof:
The proof of the main theorem proceeds by providing the explicit witness function `digraph_local_four_witness` on the domain `Fin 24` and verifying each required property.

### Structure of the Witness Graph

The 24 vertices are partitioned into two sets:
1. An 8-vertex core $C = \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\}$.
2. A 16-vertex set of sink leaves $L = \{8, 9, \dots, 23\}$.

The core subgraph induced on $C$ is a 2-outregular and 2-inregular oriented graph:
- Out-arcs between core vertices:
  $0 \to 4, 5$;
  $1 \to 3, 7$;
  $2 \to 0, 6$;
  $3 \to 2, 4$;
  $4 \to 2, 7$;
  $5 \to 1, 6$;
  $6 \to 0, 1$;
  $7 \to 3, 5$.
- In-arcs to core vertices:
  Vertex 0 receives arcs from 2, 6.
  Vertex 1 receives arcs from 5, 6.
  Vertex 2 receives arcs from 3, 4.
  Vertex 3 receives arcs from 1, 7.
  Vertex 4 receives arcs from 0, 3.
  Vertex 5 receives arcs from 0, 7.
  Vertex 6 receives arcs from 2, 5.
  Vertex 7 receives arcs from 1, 4.

Each core vertex $i \in \{0, \dots, 7\}$ has two private sink leaves:
$0 \to \{8, 9\}$,
$1 \to \{10, 11\}$,
$2 \to \{12, 13\}$,
$3 \to \{14, 15\}$,
$4 \to \{16, 17\}$,
$5 \to \{18, 19\}$,
$6 \to \{20, 21\}$,
$7 \to \{22, 23\}$.
All leaves $l \in L$ have outdegree 0 and indegree 1.

### Verification of Basic Digraph Axioms

We establish the structural axioms via the following lemmas:

\begin{lemma}[Loopless]
For every $v \in \text{Fin } 24$, $v \notin \text{out}(v)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each core vertex $i \in \{0, \dots, 7\}$, the explicit set $\text{out}(i)$ does not contain $i$. For each leaf $l \in \{8, \dots, 23\}$, $\text{out}(l) = \emptyset$, so $l \notin \emptyset$. In Lean, this is verified exhaustively by `intro v; fin_cases v <;> decide`.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Source-Free]
For every $v \in \text{Fin } 24$, there exists $u \in \text{Fin } 24$ such that $v \in \text{out}(u)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For every core vertex $i \in \{0, \dots, 7\}$, we exhibited above two distinct core in-neighbors (e.g., $0 \in \text{out}(2)$ and $0 \in \text{out}(6)$). For each leaf $l \in \{8, \dots, 23\}$, $l$ has a unique parent core vertex $\lfloor (l - 8) / 2 \rfloor$ whose out-neighborhood contains $l$. Thus every vertex has an in-neighbor, and the digraph is source-free. In Lean, this is verified by `intro v; fin_cases v <;> decide`.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Oriented]
For all $u, v \in \text{Fin } 24$, if $v \in \text{out}(u)$, then $u \notin \text{out}(v)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
If $v$ is a leaf, $\text{out}(v) = \emptyset$, so $u \notin \text{out}(v)$ holds vacuously. If both $u$ and $v$ are core vertices, we inspect all 16 directed edges between core vertices:
$(0,4), (0,5), (1,3), (1,7), (2,0), (2,6), (3,2), (3,4), (4,2), (4,7), (5,1), (5,6), (6,0), (6,1), (7,3), (7,5)$.
None of the reverse pairs are present. For instance, $4 \in \text{out}(0)$ but $\text{out}(4) = \{2, 7, 16, 17\}$, which does not contain 0. In Lean, the finite check on all $24 \times 24 = 576$ pairs is dispatched by `intro u v; fin_cases u <;> fin_cases v <;> decide`.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Maximum Outdegree Four]
For every $v \in \text{Fin } 24$, $|\text{out}(v)| \le 4$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For $v \in \{0, \dots, 7\}$, $|\text{out}(v)| = 4$. For $v \in \{8, \dots, 23\}$, $|\text{out}(v)| = 0 \le 4$. In Lean, `intro v; fin_cases v <;> decide`.
\end{proof}

### Verification of the Source-Neighborhood Inequality

\begin{lemma}[Local Source and Expansion Sets]
For each $v \in \text{Fin } 24$, $|E(v)| = |S(v)|$ and $5|E(v)| \le 4(|S(v)| + 1)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We distinguish two cases depending on whether $v$ is a leaf or a core vertex:

1. Case $v \in L$ (leaf):
The closed out-neighborhood is $N^+[v] = \{v\} \cup \emptyset = \{v\}$. Since $v$ has outdegree 0, deleting $v$ removes no outgoing edges. In the remaining graph $G - \{v\}$, every other vertex retains all of its original in-neighbors. Because $G$ is source-free, no remaining vertex becomes a source. Thus $S(v) = \emptyset$, giving $|S(v)| = 0$.
The expansion set is $E(v) = \text{out}(v) \cup \bigcup_{u \in \emptyset} \text{out}(u) = \emptyset \cup \emptyset = \emptyset$, so $|E(v)| = 0$.
We evaluate:
\[
|E(v)| = 0 = |S(v)|, \quad \text{and} \quad 5|E(v)| = 0 \le 4(0 + 1) = 4.
\]
The equality and inequality hold for all 16 leaves.

2. Case $v \in C$ (core vertex):
We trace $v = 0$ in detail; the other seven core vertices are checked the same way.
The out-neighborhood is $\text{out}(0) = \{4, 5, 8, 9\}$, so the closed out-neighborhood is $N^+[0] = \{0, 4, 5, 8, 9\}$.
We determine which vertices in $V \setminus N^+[0]$ have all their in-neighbors inside $N^+[0]$:
- Core vertices in $V \setminus N^+[0]$ are $\{1, 2, 3, 6, 7\}$. Their in-neighbors in $G$ are:
  - Vertex 1: in-neighbors $\{5, 6\}$. Here $5 \in N^+[0]$, but $6 \notin N^+[0]$. Thus 1 retains in-neighbor 6 in $G - N^+[0]$, so $1 \notin S(0)$.
  - Vertex 2: in-neighbors $\{3, 4\}$. Here $4 \in N^+[0]$, but $3 \notin N^+[0]$. Thus 2 retains in-neighbor 3, so $2 \notin S(0)$.
  - Vertex 3: in-neighbors $\{1, 7\}$. Neither belongs to $N^+[0]$, so $3 \notin S(0)$.
  - Vertex 6: in-neighbors $\{2, 5\}$. Here $5 \in N^+[0]$, but $2 \notin N^+[0]$, so $6 \notin S(0)$.
  - Vertex 7: in-neighbors $\{1, 4\}$. Here $4 \in N^+[0]$, but $1 \notin N^+[0]$, so $7 \notin S(0)$.
  Hence, no core vertex becomes a source in $G - N^+[0]$.
- Leaves in $V \setminus N^+[0]$: Each leaf $l$ has a unique in-neighbor, namely its parent core vertex. Therefore, a leaf $l$ becomes a source in $G - N^+[0]$ if and only if its parent core vertex belongs to $N^+[0]$.
  The core vertices in $N^+[0]$ are 0, 4, and 5.
  The leaves of 0 are 8 and 9, which belong to $N^+[0]$ and are deleted.
  The leaves of 4 are 16 and 17, which lie outside $N^+[0]$. Their only in-neighbor is 4, which is in $N^+[0]$. Therefore, 16 and 17 lose all in-neighbors and belong to $S(0)$.
  The leaves of 5 are 18 and 19, which lie outside $N^+[0]$. Their only in-neighbor is 5, which is in $N^+[0]$. Therefore, 18 and 19 lose all in-neighbors and belong to $S(0)$.
  All other leaves have parents in $\{1, 2, 3, 6, 7\} \cap (V \setminus N^+[0])$, so they retain their in-neighbor and do not become sources.

Thus the local source set for $v = 0$ is exactly:
\[
S(0) = \{16, 17, 18, 19\}, \quad \text{with } |S(0)| = 4.
\]
Next, since every $u \in S(0)$ is a leaf, $\text{out}(u) = \emptyset$ for all $u \in S(0)$. The local source expansion set is therefore:
\[
E(0) = \text{out}(0) \cup \bigcup_{u \in S(0)} \text{out}(u) = \{4, 5, 8, 9\} \cup \emptyset = \{4, 5, 8, 9\}, \quad \text{with } |E(0)| = 4.
\]
We now evaluate the required relations:
\[
|E(0)| = 4 = |S(0)|,
\]
and
\[
5 |E(0)| = 5 \times 4 = 20, \quad 4 (|S(0)| + 1) = 4 \times (4 + 1) = 20.
\]
Thus $5|E(0)| \le 4(|S(0)| + 1)$ holds with exact equality.
For every core vertex $v$ the same check shows that no core vertex outside $N^+[v]$ has all its in-neighbours in $N^+[v]$, so $S(v)$ consists of the four private sinks of the two core out-neighbours of $v$; for example $S(1) = \{14, 15, 22, 23\}$ and $S(6) = \{8, 9, 10, 11\}$. Since these are sinks, $E(v) = N^+(v)$, and $|S(v)| = |E(v)| = 4$.

In Lean, both the equality and the inequality for each $v \in \text{Fin } 24$ are verified by:
`intro v; fin_cases v <;> constructor <;> decide`.
\end{proof}

### Verification of the Quasi-Kernel of Size Six

\begin{lemma}[Quasi-Kernel Existence]
The set $Q = \{0, 1, 12, 13, 20, 21\} \subset \text{Fin } 24$ is an independent set of size 6 that is two-step out-dominating.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We verify the three conditions:
1. Cardinality: The six elements $0, 1, 12, 13, 20, 21$ are pairwise distinct, so $|Q| = 6$.
2. Independence: We check that no edge exists between any two elements of $Q$:
   - For $u = 0$: $\text{out}(0) = \{4, 5, 8, 9\}$, which is disjoint from $Q$.
   - For $u = 1$: $\text{out}(1) = \{3, 7, 10, 11\}$, which is disjoint from $Q$.
   - For $u \in \{12, 13, 20, 21\}$: $\text{out}(u) = \emptyset$, so no edges leave these vertices.
   Thus, for all $u, v \in Q$ with $u \neq v$, $v \notin \text{out}(u)$.
3. Two-step out-domination: Every vertex $v \in \text{Fin } 24$ is reachable from $Q$ in at most 2 steps:
   - Vertices in $Q$ (distance 0): $0, 1, 12, 13, 20, 21$.
   - Core vertices reached in 1 step:
     From 0: vertices 4 and 5.
     From 1: vertices 3 and 7.
   - Core vertices reached in 2 steps:
     From $0 \to 4 \to 2$, vertex 2 is reached.
     From $0 \to 5 \to 6$, vertex 6 is reached.
     Therefore, all eight core vertices $\{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\}$ are reached from $\{0, 1\} \subseteq Q$ in at most 2 steps.
   - Leaf vertices:
     - Leaves of 0: $\{8, 9\}$ are reached in 1 step from 0 ($0 \to 8, 9$).
     - Leaves of 1: $\{10, 11\}$ are reached in 1 step from 1 ($1 \to 10, 11$).
     - Leaves of 3: $\{14, 15\}$ are reached in 2 steps from 1 ($1 \to 3 \to 14, 15$).
     - Leaves of 4: $\{16, 17\}$ are reached in 2 steps from 0 ($0 \to 4 \to 16, 17$).
     - Leaves of 5: $\{18, 19\}$ are reached in 2 steps from 0 ($0 \to 5 \to 18, 19$).
     - Leaves of 7: $\{22, 23\}$ are reached in 2 steps from 1 ($1 \to 7 \to 22, 23$).
     - Leaves of 2: $\{12, 13\}$ are directly in $Q$ (distance 0).
     - Leaves of 6: $\{20, 21\}$ are directly in $Q$ (distance 0).
   Hence, every vertex of $\text{Fin } 24$ is at distance at most 2 from $Q$.

In Lean, this check is discharged by `refine ⟨{0,1,12,13,20,21}, by decide, by decide, fun v => by fin_cases v <;> decide⟩`.
\end{proof}

Combining these lemmas completes the Lean proof of `digraph_four_outdegree_five_four_counterexample`.
discussion:
The graph shows $f(4) \ge 5/4$ in Problem 5.2 of arXiv:2601.11847, and so that the least $d$ with $f(d) > 1$ is at most four. It is the paper's own construction for Proposition 2.3 with a different core: the paper's regular tournaments reach a ratio above 1 first at out-degree five, while a 2-diregular oriented core on eight vertices, in which no core vertex outside $N^+[v]$ has all its in-neighbours in $N^+[v]$, already works at out-degree four. Every vertex fails the criterion with constant 1, although the graph has a quasi-kernel of size $n/4$.

Several questions remain.

1. The case $d = 3$. Conjecture 5.1 of the paper asserts $f(3) \le 1$. The construction used here cannot refute it: with core in- and out-degree $c$, $k$ private sinks per core vertex, and no core vertex becoming a source, the ratio at a core vertex is $(ck+1)/(c+k)$, which exceeds 1 only when $c, k \ge 2$, that is at out-degree at least four. Whether $d = 4$ is the threshold therefore rests on Conjecture 5.1.

2. The exact value of $f(4)$. The graph gives only a lower bound; whether some sourceless oriented graph of maximum out-degree four forces a constant above $5/4$, and whether any finite constant suffices at $d = 4$, is open.

3. Growth in $d$. The same family with $c = k = d/2$ gives $f(d) \ge (d^2/4 + 1)/d$ whenever a suitable $d/2$-diregular core exists, so $f(d)$ grows at least linearly; this is the quantitative content of Proposition 2.3. We have not formalized the general family.
preliminaries:
We work in finite directed graph theory. All vertices are elements of the standard finite type `Fin 24`, representing the integers $0, 1, \dots, 23$. A directed graph is specified by an out-neighborhood function $\text{out} : V \to \text{Finset } V$.

\begin{definition}[Loopless Digraph]
A directed graph specified by $\text{out} : V \to \text{Finset } V$ is loopless if no vertex belongs to its own out-neighborhood:
\[
\forall v \in V,\ v \notin \text{out}(v).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Source-Free Digraph]
A directed graph is source-free (or has minimum in-degree at least 1) if every vertex has at least one in-neighbor:
\[
\forall v \in V,\ \exists u \in V,\ v \in \text{out}(u).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oriented Digraph]
A directed graph is oriented (or asymmetric) if it contains no directed 2-cycles:
\[
\forall u, v \in V,\ v \in \text{out}(u) \implies u \notin \text{out}(v).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Maximum Outdegree]
The maximum outdegree of the digraph is at most $d$ if for every vertex $v \in V$, the cardinality of its out-neighborhood satisfies $|\text{out}(v)| \le d$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local Source Set `digraph_local_source_set`]
For a finite type $\alpha$ with decidable equality and an out-neighborhood map $\text{out} : \alpha \to \text{Finset } \alpha$, the local source set $S(v)$ associated with a vertex $v \in \alpha$ is the set of all vertices $u \in \alpha$ outside the closed out-neighborhood $N^+[v] = \{v\} \cup \text{out}(v)$ that have no in-neighbors outside $N^+[v]$. In Lean:
```lean
def digraph_local_source_set {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (out : α → Finset α) (v : α) : Finset α :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun u => u ≠ v ∧ u ∉ out v ∧
    ∀ p, p ≠ v → p ∉ out v → u ∉ out p
```
In standard graph-theoretic notation, $u \in S(v)$ if and only if $u \notin N^+[v]$ and in the induced subgraph $G - N^+[v]$, the in-degree of $u$ is zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local Source Expansion `digraph_local_source_expansion`]
The local source expansion set $E(v)$ associated with a vertex $v$ is the union of the out-neighborhood $\text{out}(v)$ and the out-neighborhoods of all vertices in $S(v)$:
```lean
def digraph_local_source_expansion {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (out : α → Finset α) (v : α) : Finset α :=
  out v ∪ Finset.univ.filter (fun w => ∃ u ∈ digraph_local_source_set out v, w ∈ out u)
```
In formula notation, $E(v) = N^+(v) \cup \bigcup_{u \in S(v)} N^+(u)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Quasi-Kernel]
A subset $Q \subseteq V$ is a quasi-kernel of the directed graph if it satisfies two conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Independent set: for all $u, v \in Q$ with $u \neq v$, $v \notin \text{out}(u)$.
\item Two-step out-dominating set: for every vertex $v \in V$, either $v \in Q$, or $v \in \text{out}(u)$ for some $u \in Q$, or there exists $w \in \text{out}(u)$ such that $v \in \text{out}(w)$ for some $u \in Q$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The 24-Vertex Witness `digraph_local_four_witness`]
The function `digraph_local_four_witness : Fin 24 → Finset (Fin 24)` defines the out-neighborhoods of the 24 vertices as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item Core vertices $\{0, 1, \dots, 7\}$:
  \begin{align*}
  \text{out}(0) &= \{4, 5, 8, 9\}, & \text{out}(1) &= \{3, 7, 10, 11\}, \\
  \text{out}(2) &= \{0, 6, 12, 13\}, & \text{out}(3) &= \{2, 4, 14, 15\}, \\
  \text{out}(4) &= \{2, 7, 16, 17\}, & \text{out}(5) &= \{1, 6, 18, 19\}, \\
  \text{out}(6) &= \{0, 1, 20, 21\}, & \text{out}(7) &= \{3, 5, 22, 23\}.
  \end{align*}
\item Leaf vertices $\{8, 9, \dots, 23\}$: $\text{out}(v) = \emptyset$ for all $v \ge 8$.
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}

A remark on conventions: the local source set $S(v)$ only considers vertices strictly outside the closed out-neighborhood $N^+[v]$; vertices in $N^+(v)$ are deleted along with $v$. If $v$ is a leaf, $N^+[v] = \{v\}$, and since no vertex had $v$ as an in-neighbor, $S(v) = \emptyset$ and $E(v) = \emptyset$. For empty sets, $|E(v)| = |S(v)| = 0$, and the inequality $5(0) \le 4(0 + 1)$ trivially holds as $0 \le 4$.
research: An explicit source-free oriented graph of maximum outdegree four gives f(4) at least 5/4 for the uniform source-neighborhood inequality in arXiv:2601.11847, Problem 5.2, while itself having a small quasi-kernel
tier_why: One explicit graph at one degree, d = 4, by the paper's own Proposition 2.3 construction with a 2-diregular oriented core in place of a tournament; it gives f(4) >= 5/4 and so least d with f(d) > 1 is at most 4 (exactly 4 under the paper's Conjecture 5.1), a lower bound, not an exact value.

zh.title: 一个表明拟核源邻域问题中 f(4) ≥ 5/4 的 24 顶点定向图
zh.abstract: 对于无源有向图的一个顶点 $v$，令 $S(v)$ 为 $D - N^+[v]$ 的源点集，并令 $E(v) = N^+(v) \cup N^+(S(v))$。arXiv:2601.11847 的问题 5.2 询问，对每个 $d \ge 2$，使得每个最大出度至多为 $d$ 的无源定向图都存在一个满足 $f(d)|E(v)| \ge |S(v)| + 1$ 的顶点 $v$ 的最小常数 $f(d)$ 是多少，以及使得 $f(d) > 1$ 的最小 $d$ 是多少。我们给出了一个显式的 24 顶点、最大出度为 4 的无环无源定向图，其中每个顶点均满足 $5|E(v)| \le 4(|S(v)|+1)$：8 个非汇点满足 $|S(v)| = |E(v)| = 4$，16 个汇点满足 $S(v) = E(v) = \emptyset$。因此 $f(4) \ge 5/4$，且使 $f(d) > 1$ 的最小 $d$ 至多为 4；若该论文的猜想 5.1（常数为 1 的 $d = 3$ 情形）成立，则它恰为 4。该图是论文命题 2.3 构造的一个实例（将汇叶点附加到正则核上），用一个 8 顶点的 2-双正则定向核代替了正则竞赛图（原构造需要至少 7 个顶点的正则竞赛图才能使比值超过 1）。同一个图具有一个 6 顶点的拟核。所有性质均在 Lean 4 中得到验证。
zh.introduction:
有向图 $D$ 的拟核是一个独立集 $Q$，使得每个顶点都可以从 $Q$ 通过一条长度至多为 2 的有向路径到达。每个有向图都存在拟核，而小拟核猜想断言，每个具有 $n$ 个顶点的无源有向图都有一个大小至多为 $n/2$ 的拟核。

论文 arXiv:2601.11847 通过极小反例来研究该猜想。对于一个顶点 $v$，删除闭出邻域 $N^+[v] = \{v\} \cup N^+(v)$ 可能会产生源点；将 $D - N^+[v]$ 的源点集记为 $S(v)$，且
\[
E(v) = N^+(v) \cup N^+(S(v)).
\]
其算法 1 利用顶点 $v$ 和一个较小无源有向图的拟核构造出拟核，由此得到的判定准则是：若每个无源有向图都存在一个满足 $t|E(v)| \ge |S(v)| + 1$ 的顶点，则可以得到大小至多为 $tn/(t+1)$ 的拟核，因此 $t = 1$ 将给出该猜想。该论文以此方式证明了最大出度为 3 时的 $4n/7$ 界，猜想（猜想 5.1）每个最大出度至多为 3 的无源定向图都存在一个满足 $|E(v)| \ge |S(v)| + 1$ 的顶点，并指出（命题 2.3）在没有度数界限时不存在通用的常数：对任意 $c > 0$，都存在一个无源有向图，其中每个非汇点都满足 $c|E(v)| < |S(v)| + 1$。

该论文的问题 5.2 询问在有界度数下该方法能走多远：对于固定的 $d \ge 2$，使得每个最大出度至多为 $d$ 的无源定向图都存在一个顶点 $v$ 满足
\[
f(d)\,|E(v)| \ge |S(v)| + 1,
\]
的最小常数 $f(d)$ 是多少？以及使得 $f(d) > 1$ 的最小 $d$ 是多少？下界 $f(d) \ge c$ 对应于单个最大出度至多为 $d$ 的无源定向图，其中没有任何顶点对任何小于 $c$ 的常数满足该不等式。

命题 2.3 背后的构造取一个 $2n+1$ 个顶点的正则竞赛图，其中不存在出邻域等于入邻域的情况，并在每个顶点上附加 $k$ 个私有汇点；这样每个非汇点都有 $|S(v)| = nk$ 以及 $|E(v)| = n + k$，因此在出度为 $n + k$ 时的比值为 $(nk+1)/(n+k)$。该比值仅在 $n, k \ge 2$ 时大于 1；对于 $n = 2$，5 个顶点的正则竞赛图存在一个顶点的出邻域等于另一个顶点的入邻域，因此最小的情形是每个顶点带有两个汇点的 7 顶点佩利竞赛图，这给出了 $f(5) \ge 7/5$。

我们将其度数降低了一度。用一个每个顶点入度和出度均为 2 的 8 顶点定向图代替竞赛图，并在每个核顶点上附加两个私有汇点，得到一个最大出度为 4 的 24 顶点无源定向图，其中每个核顶点均有 $|S(v)| = |E(v)| = 4$，每个汇点均有 $S(v) = E(v) = \emptyset$。Lean 定理 `digraph_four_outdegree_five_four_counterexample` 指出，每个顶点都满足 $5|E(v)| \le 4(|S(v)|+1)$。因此 $f(4) \ge 5/4$，且使 $f(d) > 1$ 的最小 $d$ 至多为 4。由于最大出度至多为 2 的图其最大出度也至多为 3，猜想 5.1 将给出 $f(2), f(3) \le 1$，进而此时最小的此类 $d$ 恰为 4。该定理还在同一个图中展示了一个 6 顶点的拟核，因此局部判定准则在此处的失效并不构成对猜想本身的否定。
zh.preliminaries:
我们在有限有向图理论中展开工作。所有顶点均为标准有限类型 `Fin 24` 的元素，代表整数 $0, 1, \dots, 23$。有向图由出邻域函数 $\text{out} : V \to \text{Finset } V$ 给出。

\begin{definition}[Loopless Digraph]
由 $\text{out} : V \to \text{Finset } V$ 指定的有向图是无环的，若没有任何顶点属于其自身的出邻域：
\[
\forall v \in V,\ v \notin \text{out}(v).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Source-Free Digraph]
有向图是无源的（或最小入度至少为 1），若每个顶点都至少有一个入邻点：
\[
\forall v \in V,\ \exists u \in V,\ v \in \text{out}(u).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oriented Digraph]
有向图是定向的（或不对称的），若它不包含有向 2-圈：
\[
\forall u, v \in V,\ v \in \text{out}(u) \implies u \notin \text{out}(v).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Maximum Outdegree]
有向图的最大出度至多为 $d$，若对每个顶点 $v \in V$，其出邻域的基数满足 $|\text{out}(v)| \le d$。
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local Source Set `digraph_local_source_set`]
对于具有可判定相等性的有限类型 $\alpha$ 及出邻域映射 $\text{out} : \alpha \to \text{Finset } \alpha$，与顶点 $v \in \alpha$ 关联的局部源点集 $S(v)$ 是闭出邻域 $N^+[v] = \{v\} \cup \text{out}(v)$ 之外所有在 $N^+[v]$ 之外没有入邻点的顶点 $u \in \alpha$ 的集合。在 Lean 中：
```lean
def digraph_local_source_set {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (out : α → Finset α) (v : α) : Finset α :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun u => u ≠ v ∧ u ∉ out v ∧
    ∀ p, p ≠ v → p ∉ out v → u ∉ out p
```
用标准图论符号表示，$u \in S(v)$ 当且仅当 $u \notin N^+[v]$ 且在导出子图 $G - N^+[v]$ 中，$u$ 的入度为零。
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local Source Expansion `digraph_local_source_expansion`]
与顶点 $v$ 关联的局部源点扩张集 $E(v)$ 是出邻域 $\text{out}(v)$ 与 $S(v)$ 中所有顶点的出邻域的并集：
```lean
def digraph_local_source_expansion {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (out : α → Finset α) (v : α) : Finset α :=
  out v ∪ Finset.univ.filter (fun w => ∃ u ∈ digraph_local_source_set out v, w ∈ out u)
```
用公式符号表示即 $E(v) = N^+(v) \cup \bigcup_{u \in S(v)} N^+(u)$。
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Quasi-Kernel]
子集 $Q \subseteq V$ 是有向图的拟核，若它满足以下两个条件：
\begin{enumerate}
\item 独立集：对所有满足 $u \neq v$ 的 $u, v \in Q$，$v \notin \text{out}(u)$。
\item 两步出支配集：对每个顶点 $v \in V$，要么 $v \in Q$，要么对某个 $u \in Q$ 有 $v \in \text{out}(u)$，要么存在某个 $u \in Q$ 使得对某个 $w \in \text{out}(u)$ 有 $v \in \text{out}(w)$。
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The 24-Vertex Witness `digraph_local_four_witness`]
函数 `digraph_local_four_witness : Fin 24 → Finset (Fin 24)` 如下定义 24 个顶点的出邻域：
\begin{itemize}
\item 核顶点 $\{0, 1, \dots, 7\}$：
  \begin{align*}
  \text{out}(0) &= \{4, 5, 8, 9\}, & \text{out}(1) &= \{3, 7, 10, 11\}, \\
  \text{out}(2) &= \{0, 6, 12, 13\}, & \text{out}(3) &= \{2, 4, 14, 15\}, \\
  \text{out}(4) &= \{2, 7, 16, 17\}, & \text{out}(5) &= \{1, 6, 18, 19\}, \\
  \text{out}(6) &= \{0, 1, 20, 21\}, & \text{out}(7) &= \{3, 5, 22, 23\}.
  \end{align*}
\item 叶顶点 $\{8, 9, \dots, 23\}$：对所有 $v \ge 8$，$\text{out}(v) = \emptyset$。
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}

关于约定的说明：局部源点集 $S(v)$ 仅考虑严格位于闭出邻域 $N^+[v]$ 之外的顶点；$N^+(v)$ 中的顶点连同 $v$ 一起被删除。若 $v$ 是叶节点，则 $N^+[v] = \{v\}$，由于没有任何顶点以 $v$ 为入邻点，因此 $S(v) = \emptyset$ 且 $E(v) = \emptyset$。对于空集，$|E(v)| = |S(v)| = 0$，不等式 $5(0) \le 4(0 + 1)$ 作为 $0 \le 4$ 平凡成立。
zh.result:
在 Lean 4 中建立并验证的主要定理是 24 顶点见证图的存在性：

\begin{theorem}[`digraph_four_outdegree_five_four_counterexample`]
存在一个出邻域函数 $\text{out} : \text{Fin } 24 \to \text{Finset } (\text{Fin } 24)$ 定义了一个有向图，使得：
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\text{out}$ 是无环的：$\forall v,\ v \notin \text{out}(v)$。
\item $\text{out}$ 是无源的：$\forall v,\ \exists u,\ v \in \text{out}(u)$。
\item $\text{out}$ 是定向的：$\forall u, v,\ v \in \text{out}(u) \implies u \notin \text{out}(v)$。
\item 最大出度至多为 4：$\forall v,\ |\text{out}(v)| \le 4$。
\item 对每个顶点 $v$，局部源点集 $S(v)$ 和局部源点扩张集 $E(v)$ 满足：
\[
|E(v)| = |S(v)| \quad \text{且} \quad 5 |E(v)| \le 4 (|S(v)| + 1).
\]
\item 存在一个基数恰为 6 的独立两步出支配集 $Q \subseteq \text{Fin } 24$：
\[
|Q| = 6 \quad \text{且} \quad (\forall u, v \in Q,\ u \neq v \implies v \notin \text{out}(u))
\]
\[
\text{且} \quad (\forall v,\ \exists u \in Q,\ u = v \lor v \in \text{out}(u) \lor \exists w \in \text{out}(u),\ v \in \text{out}(w)).
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

在 Lean 4 中，该定理陈述为：
```lean
theorem digraph_four_outdegree_five_four_counterexample :
    ∃ out : Fin 24 → Finset (Fin 24),
      (∀ v, v ∉ out v) ∧
      (∀ v, ∃ u, v ∈ out u) ∧
      (∀ u v, v ∈ out u → u ∉ out v) ∧
      (∀ v, (out v).card ≤ 4) ∧
      (∀ v, (digraph_local_source_expansion out v).card = (digraph_local_source_set out v).card ∧
        5 * (digraph_local_source_expansion out v).card ≤ 4 * ((digraph_local_source_set out v).card + 1)) ∧
      (∃ Q : Finset (Fin 24), Q.card = 6 ∧
        (∀ u ∈ Q, ∀ v ∈ Q, u ≠ v → v ∉ out u) ∧
        (∀ v, ∃ u ∈ Q, u = v ∨ v ∈ out u ∨ ∃ w, w ∈ out u ∧ v ∈ out w))
```
Lean 公式化断言了在 24 元类型 `Fin 24` 上存在一个出邻域映射，合取验证了五个结构性条件以及 6 元拟核 $Q$ 的存在性。

问题 5.2 寻找满足 $f|E(v)| \ge |S(v)| + 1$ 的顶点。在此图中，当 $f < 5/4$ 时没有任何顶点满足该式：在汇点处，$|E(v)| = 0 < 1 = |S(v)| + 1$；在核顶点处，由定理可知，由于 $|E(v)| = 4 > 0$，故有 $f|E(v)| < \tfrac54|E(v)| \le |S(v)| + 1$。因此 $f(4) \ge 5/4$；在核顶点处 $5|E(v)| = 20 = 4(|S(v)|+1)$，所以常数 $5/4$ 本身在该图上达到，使用该图无法改进此界。特别地，$f(4) > 1$，因此问题 5.2 中使 $f(d) > 1$ 的最小 $d$ 至多为 4。拟核 $Q$ 具有 $6 = 24/4$ 个顶点，完全在猜想的 $n/2$ 范围内。
zh.proof:
主定理的证明通过在定义域 `Fin 24` 上给出显式的见证函数 `digraph_local_four_witness` 并验证每一项所需性质来进行。

### 见证图的结构

这 24 个顶点被划分为两个集合：
1. 一个 8 顶点核 $C = \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\}$。
2. 一个 16 顶点汇叶点集 $L = \{8, 9, \dots, 23\}$。

在 $C$ 上导出的核子图是一个 2-出正则且 2-入正则的定向图：
- 核顶点之间的出弧：
  $0 \to 4, 5$；
  $1 \to 3, 7$；
  $2 \to 0, 6$；
  $3 \to 2, 4$；
  $4 \to 2, 7$；
  $5 \to 1, 6$；
  $6 \to 0, 1$；
  $7 \to 3, 5$。
- 指向核顶点的入弧：
  顶点 0 接收来自 2, 6 的弧。
  顶点 1 接收来自 5, 6 的弧。
  顶点 2 接收来自 3, 4 的弧。
  顶点 3 接收来自 1, 7 的弧。
  顶点 4 接收来自 0, 3 的弧。
  顶点 5 接收来自 0, 7 的弧。
  顶点 6 接收来自 2, 5 的弧。
  顶点 7 接收来自 1, 4 的弧。

每个核顶点 $i \in \{0, \dots, 7\}$ 都有两个私有汇叶点：
$0 \to \{8, 9\}$，
$1 \to \{10, 11\}$，
$2 \to \{12, 13\}$，
$3 \to \{14, 15\}$，
$4 \to \{16, 17\}$，
$5 \to \{18, 19\}$，
$6 \to \{20, 21\}$，
$7 \to \{22, 23\}$。
所有叶点 $l \in L$ 的出度均为 0，入度均为 1。

### 基本有向图公理的验证

我们通过以下引理建立结构公理：

\begin{lemma}[Loopless]
对每个 $v \in \text{Fin } 24$，$v \notin \text{out}(v)$。
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
对每个核顶点 $i \in \{0, \dots, 7\}$，显式集合 $\text{out}(i)$ 不包含 $i$。对每个叶点 $l \in \{8, \dots, 23\}$，$\text{out}(l) = \emptyset$，故 $l \notin \emptyset$。在 Lean 中，这通过 `intro v; fin_cases v <;> decide` 穷举验证。
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Source-Free]
对每个 $v \in \text{Fin } 24$，存在 $u \in \text{Fin } 24$ 使得 $v \in \text{out}(u)$。
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
对每个核顶点 $i \in \{0, \dots, 7\}$，我们在上文展示了两个不同的核入邻点（例如 $0 \in \text{out}(2)$ 且 $0 \in \text{out}(6)$）。对每个叶点 $l \in \{8, \dots, 23\}$，$l$ 都有唯一的父核顶点 $\lfloor (l - 8) / 2 \rfloor$，其出邻域包含 $l$。因此每个顶点都有入邻点，有向图是无源的。在 Lean 中，这通过 `intro v; fin_cases v <;> decide` 验证。
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Oriented]
对所有 $u, v \in \text{Fin } 24$，若 $v \in \text{out}(u)$，则 $u \notin \text{out}(v)$。
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
若 $v$ 是叶点，则 $\text{out}(v) = \emptyset$，故 $u \notin \text{out}(v)$ 平凡成立。若 $u$ 和 $v$ 均为核顶点，我们检查核顶点之间的所有 16 条有向边：
$(0,4), (0,5), (1,3), (1,7), (2,0), (2,6), (3,2), (3,4), (4,2), (4,7), (5,1), (5,6), (6,0), (6,1), (7,3), (7,5)$。
其中不存在任何反向对。例如，$4 \in \text{out}(0)$，但 $\text{out}(4) = \{2, 7, 16, 17\}$，不包含 0。在 Lean 中，对所有 $24 \times 24 = 576$ 对顶点的有限检验由 `intro u v; fin_cases u <;> fin_cases v <;> decide` 完成。
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Maximum Outdegree Four]
对每个 $v \in \text{Fin } 24$，$|\text{out}(v)| \le 4$。
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
对 $v \in \{0, \dots, 7\}$，$|\text{out}(v)| = 4$。对 $v \in \{8, \dots, 23\}$，$|\text{out}(v)| = 0 \le 4$。在 Lean 中，通过 `intro v; fin_cases v <;> decide` 验证。
\end{proof}

### 源邻域不等式的验证

\begin{lemma}[Local Source and Expansion Sets]
对每个 $v \in \text{Fin } 24$，$|E(v)| = |S(v)|$ 且 $5|E(v)| \le 4(|S(v)| + 1)$。
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
根据 $v$ 是叶点还是核顶点，我们分两种情况进行讨论：

1. 情形 $v \in L$（叶点）：
闭出邻域为 $N^+[v] = \{v\} \cup \emptyset = \{v\}$。由于 $v$ 的出度为 0，删除 $v$ 不会移除任何出边。在剩余图 $G - \{v\}$ 中，每个其他顶点都保留其所有原有的入邻点。因为 $G$ 是无源的，所以剩余顶点均未成为源点。因此 $S(v) = \emptyset$，即 $|S(v)| = 0$。
扩张集为 $E(v) = \text{out}(v) \cup \bigcup_{u \in \emptyset} \text{out}(u) = \emptyset \cup \emptyset = \emptyset$，故 $|E(v)| = 0$。
计算得：
\[
|E(v)| = 0 = |S(v)|, \quad \text{且} \quad 5|E(v)| = 0 \le 4(0 + 1) = 4.
\]
等式与不等式对所有 16 个叶点均成立。

2. 情形 $v \in C$（核顶点）：
我们详细考察 $v = 0$；其余 7 个核顶点的检验方式相同。
出邻域为 $\text{out}(0) = \{4, 5, 8, 9\}$，因此闭出邻域为 $N^+[0] = \{0, 4, 5, 8, 9\}$。
我们确定 $V \setminus N^+[0]$ 中哪些顶点的所有入邻点都在 $N^+[0]$ 内：
- $V \setminus N^+[0]$ 中的核顶点为 $\{1, 2, 3, 6, 7\}$。它们在 $G$ 中的入邻点为：
  - 顶点 1：入邻点 $\{5, 6\}$。这里 $5 \in N^+[0]$，但 $6 \notin N^+[0]$。因此 1 在 $G - N^+[0]$ 中保留了入邻点 6，所以 $1 \notin S(0)$。
  - 顶点 2：入邻点 $\{3, 4\}$。这里 $4 \in N^+[0]$，但 $3 \notin N^+[0]$。因此 2 保留了入邻点 3，所以 $2 \notin S(0)$。
  - 顶点 3：入邻点 $\{1, 7\}$。两者均不属于 $N^+[0]$，所以 $3 \notin S(0)$。
  - 顶点 6：入邻点 $\{2, 5\}$。这里 $5 \in N^+[0]$，但 $2 \notin N^+[0]$，所以 $6 \notin S(0)$。
  - 顶点 7：入邻点 $\{1, 4\}$。这里 $4 \in N^+[0]$，但 $1 \notin N^+[0]$，所以 $7 \notin S(0)$。
  因此，在 $G - N^+[0]$ 中没有核顶点成为源点。
- $V \setminus N^+[0]$ 中的叶点：每个叶点 $l$ 都有唯一的入邻点，即其父核顶点。因此，叶点 $l$ 在 $G - N^+[0]$ 中成为源点当且仅当其父核顶点属于 $N^+[0]$。
  $N^+[0]$ 中的核顶点为 0、4 和 5。
  0 的叶点为 8 和 9，它们属于 $N^+[0]$ 且已被删除。
  4 的叶点为 16 和 17，位于 $N^+[0]$ 之外。它们唯一的入邻点是 4，且 $4 \in N^+[0]$。因此，16 和 17 失去了所有入邻点，属于 $S(0)$。
  5 的叶点为 18 和 19，位于 $N^+[0]$ 之外。它们唯一的入邻点是 5，且 $5 \in N^+[0]$。因此，18 和 19 失去了所有入邻点，属于 $S(0)$。
  所有其他叶点的父节点都在 $\{1, 2, 3, 6, 7\} \cap (V \setminus N^+[0])$ 中，因此它们保留了入邻点，不会成为源点。

由此，$v = 0$ 的局部源点集恰为：
\[
S(0) = \{16, 17, 18, 19\}, \quad \text{其中 } |S(0)| = 4.
\]
接着，由于每个 $u \in S(0)$ 都是叶点，对所有 $u \in S(0)$ 均有 $\text{out}(u) = \emptyset$。因此局部源点扩张集为：
\[
E(0) = \text{out}(0) \cup \bigcup_{u \in S(0)} \text{out}(u) = \{4, 5, 8, 9\} \cup \emptyset = \{4, 5, 8, 9\}, \quad \text{其中 } |E(0)| = 4.
\]
现在我们计算所需的关系：
\[
|E(0)| = 4 = |S(0)|,
\]
以及
\[
5 |E(0)| = 5 \times 4 = 20, \quad 4 (|S(0)| + 1) = 4 \times (4 + 1) = 20.
\]
因此 $5|E(0)| \le 4(|S(0)| + 1)$ 恰好取等号成立。
对每个核顶点 $v$，同样的检验表明 $N^+[v]$ 之外没有任何核顶点的所有入邻点都在 $N^+[v]$ 中，因此 $S(v)$ 由 $v$ 的两个核出邻点的 4 个私有汇点组成；例如 $S(1) = \{14, 15, 22, 23\}$ 以及 $S(6) = \{8, 9, 10, 11\}$。由于这些点都是汇点，故 $E(v) = N^+(v)$，且 $|S(v)| = |E(v)| = 4$。

在 Lean 中，对每个 $v \in \text{Fin } 24$ 的等式与不等式均通过以下方式验证：
`intro v; fin_cases v <;> constructor <;> decide`。
\end{proof}

### 大小为 6 的拟核的验证

\begin{lemma}[Quasi-Kernel Existence]
集合 $Q = \{0, 1, 12, 13, 20, 21\} \subset \text{Fin } 24$ 是一个大小为 6 的独立两步出支配集。
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
我们验证这三个条件：
1. 基数：六个元素 $0, 1, 12, 13, 20, 21$ 两两互异，故 $|Q| = 6$。
2. 独立性：我们检查 $Q$ 的任意两个元素之间都不存在边：
   - 对于 $u = 0$：$\text{out}(0) = \{4, 5, 8, 9\}$，与 $Q$ 不相交。
   - 对于 $u = 1$：$\text{out}(1) = \{3, 7, 10, 11\}$，与 $Q$ 不相交。
   - 对于 $u \in \{12, 13, 20, 21\}$：$\text{out}(u) = \emptyset$，故没有从这些顶点出发的边。
   因此，对所有满足 $u \neq v$ 的 $u, v \in Q$，$v \notin \text{out}(u)$。
3. 两步出支配：$\text{Fin } 24$ 中的每个顶点 $v$ 都可以从 $Q$ 在至多 2 步内到达：
   - $Q$ 中的顶点（距离为 0）：$0, 1, 12, 13, 20, 21$。
   - 在 1 步内到达的核顶点：
     从 0 出发：顶点 4 和 5。
     从 1 出发：顶点 3 和 7。
   - 在 2 步内到达的核顶点：
     由 $0 \to 4 \to 2$ 到达顶点 2。
     由 $0 \to 5 \to 6$ 到达顶点 6。
     因此，所有 8 个核顶点 $\{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\}$ 都可以从 $\{0, 1\} \subseteq Q$ 在至多 2 步内到达。
   - 叶顶点：
     - 0 的叶点：$\{8, 9\}$ 从 0 在 1 步内到达（$0 \to 8, 9$）。
     - 1 的叶点：$\{10, 11\}$ 从 1 在 1 步内到达（$1 \to 10, 11$）。
     - 3 的叶点：$\{14, 15\}$ 从 1 在 2 步内到达（$1 \to 3 \to 14, 15$）。
     - 4 的叶点：$\{16, 17\}$ 从 0 在 2 步内到达（$0 \to 4 \to 16, 17$）。
     - 5 的叶点：$\{18, 19\}$ 从 0 在 2 步内到达（$0 \to 5 \to 18, 19$）。
     - 7 的叶点：$\{22, 23\}$ 从 1 在 2 步内到达（$1 \to 7 \to 22, 23$）。
     - 2 的叶点：$\{12, 13\}$ 直接属于 $Q$（距离为 0）。
     - 6 的叶点：$\{20, 21\}$ 直接属于 $Q$（距离为 0）。
   因此，$\text{Fin } 24$ 的每个顶点到 $Q$ 的距离至多为 2。

在 Lean 中，此项检验由 `refine ⟨{0,1,12,13,20,21}, by decide, by decide, fun v => by fin_cases v <;> decide⟩` 完成。
\end{proof}
